messages:
maria: quick flag — after HF->Redwood conversion of `sentence-transformers/model-x` we see embedding drift. Ran a small eval of 5k queries -> avg cosine down ~0.012 vs HF baseline. Not huge but consistent across datasets. Anyone else hit this after conversion?

arjun: can you paste the tokenizer/config you used? often this is special-token/truncation weirdness.

maria: pasted below — converter output + our minimal wrap: 
```json
{
  "tokenizer_config": {
    "cls_token_id": null,
    "bos_token_id": 1,
    "eos_token_id": 2,
    "pad_token_id": 0,
    "add_special_tokens": true,
    "truncation_strategy": "only_first"
  },
  "model_config": {
    "pooler_type": "cls",
    "add_pooling_layer": false
  }
}
```

maria: converter (hf->rw) defaulted truncation -> `only_first`. HF training used `longest_first` with pairwise inputs. That might cause different tokens kept when we hit max_len.

sam: also check `cls_token_id`: HF models sometimes use `bos_token` as CLS and converter mapping can drop the explicit cls token (cls_token_id null) which shifts all positions. If your reranker does CLS pooling it will pick the wrong vector.

liyah: quick diff I ran locally: tokenized outputs for same pair (truncation at 16) — HF tokenizer (transformers) vs converted Redwood tokenizer: 
```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
# HF baseline
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('sentence-transformers/model-x')
print(tok('Query text', 'Doc text', truncation=True, max_length=16, return_tensors='pt'))
# Converted RW tokenizer (loading from our converted files)
# lw = RedwoodTokenizer('...') 
# print(lw('Query text','Doc text', truncation=True,max_length=16))
```
liyah: HF token ids: [1, 45, 234, 2, 3, 900, ...] (cls/bos at start). Converted RW token ids: [45, 234, 2, 3, 900, ...] — so CLS/BOS got dropped.

arjun: that's the smoking gun. If `cls_token_id` became null / removed, and `pooler_type` is `cls`, the model returns hidden[0] which is now the first real token, not a CLS embedding. That will change embeddings a lot.

maria: ugh. Is this converter bug (dropping cls) or mismatch in expected `add_special_tokens`? We left `add_special_tokens: true` but cls_token_id null seems contradictory.

sam: two-pronged: 1) converter didn't map `cls_token` -> `bos` consistently for this HF variant. 2) truncation strategy `only_first` vs `longest_first` for pairs: HF used `longest_first` so it chops both sides; `only_first` chops only the first sequence -> when queries are short this shifts context in doc part. Both affect pooled vector.

liyah: quick repro numbers: same 5k sample, mean cosine (HF) = 0.872, (converted) = 0.860. If I force-add a synthetic CLS token to converted tokenizer (id=1 at front) and set `cls_token_id=1`, mean cosine goes back to 0.871. So cls absence explains ~0.011 of the gap. Remaining 0.001 could be truncation differences and tokenization subtleties.

arjun: good detective work. Action items: 
• fix converter mapping so cls/bos/eos mapping preserved and `cls_token_id` never null when model expects pooler_type=cls.
• default truncation strategy to HF `longest_first` when converting pairwise models (or propagate original tokenizer.truncation_strategy).
• run quick AB: converted-with-fix vs current converted on 10k evals and post to #eng-ml.

maria: assigning to @arjun? can you take converter PR and small regression run?

arjun: on it. I'll make two tiny changes: preserve `cls_token` -> `bos` mapping and keep `truncation_strategy` from HF tokenizer config. Will add a test that tokenization roundtrip keeps sentinel tokens.

sam: also add a note in onboarding checklist: if `pooler_type` is `cls` ensure `cls_token_id` exists and `add_pooling_layer` matches model weights (some HF checkpoints store a separate pooling layer).

eval-bot: regression-alert: embedding-mean-cosine-drop (model-x converted) threshold exceeded (delta=0.012). See run 2026-03-09T12:22Z — details posted to the eval dashboard.

maria: thanks. After ARJUN's fix, I'll re-run the full 100k eval. If numbers recover we can mark this as converter bug + config mismatch. If not, we'll dig deeper into tokenizer normalization options (lowercase, strip_accents) and quantization changes.

liyah: small note — we should also confirm reranker pooling config: some downstream code used `cls_pooling=True` explicitly even when model has `add_pooling_layer=false`. That double mismatch causes silent changes. I'll grep the reranker codebase for `cls_pooling` flags.

arjun: PR drafted, tests added. ping me if you want early diff. I'll post when runs finish. :thumbsup:
